questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
Guess the weight of a load on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your entire vehicle. You will explain what you are checking and why you are checking it.

questions.question: When a vehicle starts, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: After an engine starts, the coolant temperature should rise gradually until it reaches normal operating temperature.

questions.question: Exhaust system parts should be:

options.text: Rubbing against other parts of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Check that all exhaust system parts are tight and secure. Parts must not be loose, broken, or missing. They should not rub against any moving parts of the vehicle.

questions.question: If one-fourth of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing during inspection:

options.text: The driver can drive, but only at reduced speeds.
The vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.
The vehicle is fine to drive since most of the spring is still there.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: Check leaf springs for broken or missing leaves. This is a serious problem. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from any leaf spring, the vehicle must be taken out of service.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, you should:

options.text: Stay as far from the flames as possible.
Use any extinguisher on any type of fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far from the flames as possible.
questions.explanation: Stay far away from the fire. Aim the extinguisher at the base or source of the fire, not at the flames. Some fires may need water. If you are unsure how to handle a fire, wait for trained firefighters.

questions.question: To avoid slowing traffic when driving a large truck, you should:

options.text: Try to pass another vehicle while going uphill.
Stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane when possible.
questions.explanation: If your heavy load cannot keep up with other traffic, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: Hanging meat:

options.text: Should never be transported by trailer.
Must be approved by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

questions.explanation: Drive carefully when transporting hanging meat. This load is unstable because it has a high center of gravity and the swinging meat can affect how you control the vehicle.

questions.question: While going downhill, you should brake until you reach a speed that is:
questions.explanation: Going downhill, hold the brake until your vehicle reaches 5 mph below your safe speed, then release it. Repeat this process.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle set by the manufacturer
The maximum weight a vehicle can pull
The minimum weight a vehicle can carry

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle set by the manufacturer
questions.explanation: The Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum loaded weight for a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer.

questions.question: What can happen if the exhaust system does not work properly?

options.text: Poison fumes may enter the cab.
Fumes may come out the back of the muffler.
You may not be able to steer properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison fumes may enter the cab.
questions.explanation: Leaks in the exhaust system are very dangerous. They can allow toxic fumes into the cab or sleeper area, which can harm drivers and passengers.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning happen most often?

options.text: When a vehicle travels faster than 60 mph.
When tire pressure is too low.
When tire tread is too deep.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tire pressure is too low.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens most when driving on wet roads with low tire pressure and worn tread. It can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle is hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Do not apply the brakes if your vehicle hydroplanes. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This helps you regain traction.

questions.question: What is a problem with improperly loaded cargo?

options.text: It is safer than properly loaded cargo.

questions.explanation: Cargo that is not properly loaded or secured is a hazard to you and others on the road.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign of when to shift to a higher gear?
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift up: engine speed (RPM) and road speed (mph). Read your vehicle's manual to learn the correct RPM range and watch your speedometer for speed. Time of day is not an indicator for shifting.

questions.question: What can you do to avoid a hazard?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
You may need to swerve out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may need to swerve out of the way.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best option. If you don't have enough space to stop, swerving out of the way may be safer.

questions.question: What vehicles must have emergency brakes?

options.text: Vehicles with air brakes do not need them.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have both emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: When do you need an air brake endorsement?

options.text: To operate a vehicle with air brakes.
To drive any truck with a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: To operate a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You must pass an air brakes test to be licensed to drive a vehicle with air brakes, including air over hydraulic systems.

questions.question: Why must you decide quickly if your brakes fail going downhill?

options.text: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle goes.
The longer you wait, the more vehicles move out of your way.
The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle goes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle goes.
questions.explanation: Act quickly if your brakes fail on a downhill slope. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go and the harder it will be to stop.

questions.question: What should you NOT check during a vehicle inspection?

options.text: If tire air pressure is too high.
If tire air pressure is too low.
If all tires are the same brand name.

questions.correctAnswerText: If all tires are the same brand name.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that tire air pressure is not too high or too low. The tire brand name does not matter.

questions.question: When should you use your turn signal for a lane change?
questions.explanation: Always signal before you turn or change lanes.

questions.question: When you start your vehicle, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Jump quickly from cold to hot.

questions.explanation: After you start your engine, the coolant temperature should rise slowly to reach normal operating temperature.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Usually happens when vehicles travel faster than 65 mph.
Can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip on the road and slide on water instead. You do not need a lot of water for this to happen. Hydroplaning can start at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: What is the main cause of death and injury in a work zone?
questions.explanation: Speeding causes the most deaths and injuries in work zones. Be extra careful when driving near workers.

questions.question: The two markings on a front brake limiting valve usually say:
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brake systems made before 1975 have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings.

questions.question: Which gas from a faulty exhaust system is dangerous?
questions.explanation: A leaking exhaust system can let carbon monoxide, a poison, into the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: While driving, ____ holds spring brakes in place.
questions.explanation: While driving, air pressure holds spring brakes in place. If air pressure drops low enough, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: A trailer with unbalanced weight:
questions.explanation: Unbalanced weight in a trailer is unsafe to handle. Too little or too much weight on the front axle makes steering difficult. Weight should be spread evenly from front to back and side to side, and as low as possible.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT mean your brakes are bad?

options.text: Pads with no oil or grease on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads with no oil or grease on them
questions.explanation: When checking your brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil, grease, or brake fluid, and shoes that are worn dangerously thin.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Hard to focus, blinking a lot

questions.explanation: Warning signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, forgetting miles you drove, missing exits, drifting from your lane, following too closely, and hitting shoulder rumble strips.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.explanation: When used and maintained properly, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: Exhaust system parts should:
questions.explanation: Exhaust system parts must not leak. A leaking exhaust system can let poisonous fumes into the cab.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a reason to use your mirrors?

options.text: You are looking at fuel prices.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are looking at fuel prices.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. It is especially important to check them when turning, changing lanes, merging, and making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: Before backing a vehicle where there may be hanging objects, a driver should:

options.text: Cut wires or branches as needed.

questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Exit your vehicle and walk the path where you will back. Look for hazards, especially hanging objects that are hard to see in mirrors.

questions.question: Dual tires should:
questions.explanation: When inspecting a vehicle, check that dual tires do not touch one another or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: If a truck is equipped with one, a trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Stop the truck from rolling back when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the truck from rolling back when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve can prevent the truck from rolling backward when you start moving from a stop.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the air leakage rate should be no more than ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test on a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the air leakage rate must not exceed 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster, the vehicle needs repair before driving.

questions.question: When backing a vehicle with a helper, the helper should stand:

options.text: In front of the passenger's side of the vehicle.
In front of the driver's side of the vehicle.
Near the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the truck.
questions.explanation: Use a helper when backing up. The helper should stand near the back of the vehicle in a place where the driver can see them.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Always use turn signals when changing lanes.
Only use turn signals if there is a vehicle next to them.
Not use a turn signal if a lane change is obvious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes so other drivers know your intentions.

questions.question: Front tire tread depth must be at least ____ in every major groove.
questions.explanation: Front tires need a tread depth of at least 4/32 of an inch in every major groove. Other tires need at least 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle driver:

options.text: May use any cell phone while driving.
May only use a hands-free cell phone while driving, if permitted.
May only use a cell phone while driving on rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: May only use a hands-free cell phone while driving, if permitted.
questions.explanation: If you use a cell phone while driving, use only a hands-free phone placed close to you. Even hands-free phones can distract you from driving. Know all cell phone laws in your state.

questions.question: When making a tight turn in a CMV, what should the driver do?

options.text: Drive as fast as a car driver would.
Focus on the road and ignore speed.
Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind you.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not expect how slowly a CMV must go to turn safely. Brake early and slow down gradually to warn them in advance.

questions.question: When loading cargo, where should the weight be placed?

options.text: As close to the cab as possible.

questions.explanation: Placing weight as low as possible reduces the risk of the vehicle tipping over.

questions.question: What might rust around wheel nuts indicate?
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts can mean they are loose. Check their tightness before driving if you see rust near the wheel nuts.

questions.question: How does talking on a hands-free cell phone affect driving?

options.text: It allows the driver to eat while driving.

questions.explanation: A hands-free phone does not require using your hands, but talking on any phone while driving can distract you from the road.

questions.question: How should you complete an offset back/left parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left maneuver, pull straight forward first, then back up to the left. The vehicle must be completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: If you doubt there is enough space under a bridge or sign, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under overhead objects, slow down and take a different route if possible.

questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot go in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Only reverse if absolutely necessary.

questions.question: In very hot weather, why should tires be checked regularly?

options.text: Air pressure may increase with the temperature.
The tread wears down more quickly than in cooler weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase with the temperature.
questions.explanation: Air pressure increases as temperature rises. Pay special attention to tire mounting and pressure when traveling in hot weather.

questions.question: Is emergency equipment in a vehicle required?

options.text: Only for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check for emergency equipment including spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: How should an exhaust system be mounted?
questions.explanation: The exhaust system must have all parts properly mounted. Nothing should be loose, broken, missing, or rubbing against moving vehicle parts.
